scope: Remaining interruption/relaunch evidence gap only; seven prior scenarios were not rerun

scenarios.name: Stopped marker relaunch preserves recorded allocator and native copy
scenarios.observed: After fixture default changed from git to treehouse, the replacement ran in the original copy, allocator remained git, and reservation bytes and Git worktree inventory were unchanged. The same real tmux pane was reused.
scenarios.limitation: Exercises the documented already-stopped relaunch path with a non-model shell marker, not fm-control's interactive model-agent stop/checkpoint transaction. No inference or credentials were used.

scenarios.name: Failed reservation retirement after metadata removal recovers through startup replay
scenarios.interface: bin/fm-teardown.sh TASK followed by bin/fm-bootstrap.sh with FM_BOOTSTRAP_NETWORK=skip
scenarios.fault: Existing test technique: command-scoped rm wrapper refuses only the exact owned reservation path; real endpoint and filesystem operations remain in use
scenarios.observed: Teardown returned 1 after removing the copy and task metadata. The byte-identical reservation and production backlog-close marker remained. Bootstrap returned 0 and retired both remaining records. The primary project remained clean.
scenarios.limitation: Deterministically injected filesystem-operation failure, not an asynchronous process kill. The removal owner suppressed wrapper stderr, so the transcript does not retain its attempted teardown-parent PID diagnostic. Marker and tmux process identities are retained.
